notes: Culver City, CALIFORNIA — independent city in Los Angeles County (pop. ~40k, 5.0 sq mi). 8,744 shipped parcels (13,678 Assessor records), $10.29B assessed land value / $18.07B total assessed value. Source: LA County eGIS public parcel layer (public.gis.lacounty.gov/public/rest/services/LACounty_Cache/LACounty_Parcel/MapServer/0) carrying the LA County Assessor's current secured roll (Roll_Year 2026: Roll_LandValue / Roll_ImpValue / Roll_LandBaseYear / Roll_RealEstateExemp / UseCode), clipped to the county's Culver City boundary (Political_Boundaries/MapServer/19). The county's own TaxRateCity='CULVER CITY' agrees with that clip on 13,678 of 13,679 parcels. Culver City's own GIS viewer (gisproxy.culvercity.org 'Current Land Base Value') shows these same Assessor numbers; the city's open-data download has boundaries only. See run_culvercity.py.

PROP 13 — THESE ARE NOT MARKET VALUES. California assesses a parcel at its value when it last changed hands or was newly built (the 'base year value', the earliest being 1975), rising at most 2%/yr after that. Land value on this map therefore tracks WHEN a parcel last sold as much as WHERE it is. On ordinary single-family lots (one Assessor record per lot) the median assessed land value is $11.91/sqft for a 1975-79 land base year (937 lots, 16%), $37 for the 1980s, $58 for the 1990s, $104 for the 2000s, $154 for the 2010s and $238 for 2020-26 (1,097 lots) — a 7.0x gap between pre-2000 base years ($33.82/sqft, 44% of lots) and 2020+ ($238.23). Valuing every single-family lot at the 2020+ median rate would give ~$8.0B against the roll's $3.68B. So the map systematically understates long-held land and shows block-to-block noise that is sale-date, not location. The popup shows each parcel's 'Land Base Year (Prop 13)' so a low value can be read in context. Roll values are the Assessor's own published figures and ship unchanged.

The same Prop 13 effect inflates 'Underdeveloped': Culver City's land share of assessed value is high everywhere (land is $10.29B of $18.07B), so 5,531 of 8,744 parcels (63%) clear the standard land/(land+impr) cutoff (0.67 single-family, 0.50 other; the same cutoffs every city uses). That is a statement about coastal-LA land prices and Prop 13 base years, not about 63% of the city being under-built.

EXEMPTION: California puts no value on government-owned land (UseCode 88xx 'Government Parcel', Roll_LandValue NULL — 158 records) and state-assessed utility property (81xx, 28) is valued by the State Board of Equalization, not on this roll; both dropped, with 129 other value-less records. Welfare/religious/college exemptions (churches, private schools, nonprofit housing, 43 records) carry a normal roll value plus a Roll_RealEstateExemp >= 99% of it and are dropped. 1-4 unit homes are NEVER dropped on the exemption test — those are disabled veterans' exemptions, which fully cover 24 long-held low-base-year homes; dropping them would remove a taxable-class home and reveal the owner's status by omission. 77 records carrying only a nominal placeholder value (land < $1,000 and improvements < $1,000: condo/PUD common lots, pipeline and ROW strips, $9 mall-lot placeholders) are dropped as unassessed after the PUD merge below has used them.

NO OWNER NAMES: the county layer carries none (the Assessor exposes names only through its portal one record at a time). Exemption AMOUNTS are read for the exemption test and never exported (they reveal owner-occupancy and disabled-veteran status per household).

CONDOS ARE STACKED COPIES, COLLAPSED — not stubs. LA County gives every condo unit its own AIN but maps it as an identical copy of the WHOLE LOT polygon: 4,360 records sit in 132 stacks (max 404 units at Tract 23852, Green Valley Circle, Fox Hills). Each unit carries its own real land share, so each stack collapses to one parcel per lot with values SUMMED across distinct AINs. Matched on footprint overlap (IoU >= 0.95, or >= 90% cover between two condo-type records) because some units' lot copies were digitised from an older, larger lot line. Calibration: the big Fox Hills complexes land at $150-320/sqft, right on the $238 single-family 2020+ rate — units resell often, so the summed unit shares are close to current value, while the long-held rental apartment complexes next door sit at $10-30/sqft (Prop 13), which is why condo land looks 'hot' next to its neighbours.

PUD TOWNHOMES ARE MERGED DOWN onto their common land (skill §6b). The Fox Hills PUD tracts (Raintree / Tara Ter / Cascade Ct / Gaslight Ln, map book 4296, and Tract 31991 off Canterbury Dr) map each townhouse as its own ~1,250-2,600 sqft fee lot carrying the unit's land share, with the grounds/drives/pools on separate lots the Assessor carries at $9. Left alone they rendered as $600-750/sqft pencils and the grounds vanished. 275 unit lots + 10 common lots -> 4 development parcels (4.5-7.7 acres each) at $90-117/sqft. Gate = plat dominance per Assessor map page (small valued lots >= 60% of the page's valued parcels), the Provo lesson. 24 small residential lots elsewhere stay individual (ordinary small lots, no common land).
Parcel link = LA County Assessor portal detail page (portal.assessor.lacounty.gov/parceldetail/<AIN>, verified live). A merged condo/PUD parcel links to its highest-value unit.

Remnants: 15 hidden (hideRemnants; baked with --drop-remnants): 14 sub-500-sqft slivers plus AIN 4209029023, a 620 sqft 'PAR C' strip off Jefferson Blvd carrying $5.31M of land ($8,559/sqft, ~10x anything else) — a genuine Assessor record whose value belongs to the adjoining office assemblage (the Hartford 0 OLIVE ST class of anomaly).

Stale vacant codes: Ivy Station (8825 National Blvd) still carries UseCode 100V (vacant commercial) with $144M of improvements on the roll; a 'V' code with improvements > 50% of land is classed by its use family instead of Vacant.

~13.7k records / 8.7k parcels would fit the browser GeoParquet path, but baked to PMTiles + H3 like Provo (small-lot/condo cities render sparse zoomed out on GeoParquet — the Olympia lesson). H3 ladder r7/r8/r10/r11, parcels from z12.

PARKING: OSM-only (the NAIP+ML satellite path was not run), so it undercounts: 126 OSM lots / 84.6 acres inside the city, classified 107 surface (61.6 ac, ~$284M of assessed land) / 18 structure (22.9 ac) / 1 excluded (fuel forecourt); the Parking page headline (after its parcel-context filter) reads 59.4 acres / $271.7M, 2.6% of taxable land value. overpass-api.de was unreachable during the build (the fuel-station step hung twice), so it ran with OSMNX_OVERPASS_URL=https://maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api. Parking land values inherit Prop 13 (a lot held since the 1970s carries 1970s land value). The Assessor roll has its own 'Parking Lots' use (27xx commercial, 38xx industrial): 140 surface lots ship as 'Parking Lot' in the Underused tab, and 6 whose improvements exceed their land are classed 'Parking Structure' (a deck is a building — issue #12 house rule).
